scope.range: b765b55cca0e1eaacebc738a68de77906bb50756 plus current Stage B runtime migration and the direct-parent protocol refusal repair in the working tree

positive_observations: Direct-parent review-code-001 is resolved for the reproduced unsupported initial negotiation. The actual public entry and independently tested copy both match SHA-256 f734ed38cce00f14aa3229a6b21f8c7a452d6f7c2ef46f6b362907ba6aacecbd. The installed SDK resolves to ACPX 0.13.2. Its prepareInitialRuntimeRecord copies client.initializeResult.protocolVersion into the public record, and retainInitializedSessionOwner awaits the checkpoint before ensureSession returns. The entry observes that existing save contract and refuses non-v1 or unobserved negotiation before startTurn with unsupported_protocol_version and phase ensure_session. Comparison with the retained old entry shows the bounded repair reuses the SDK rather than adding another protocol engine.

AcpDriver now takes protocolVersion only from the optional numeric sibling of the result line; absent or nonnumeric values remain null. The three previous terminal-derived v1 assignments consume that observation. delegate-worker publishes the resulting observation without a requested-version fallback, and acp-conformance still requires acp_protocol_version === 1 plus a finished result and the remaining gates. The reproduced version-2 refusal therefore cannot become successful v1 conformance through the former synthetic value.

Direct-parent review-tests-002 is resolved for the same root cause, rather than being discarded as a duplicate. tests/acp-driver.test.cjs now selects UBP_TEST_ACPX_ENTRY for one actual AcpDriver regression using the existing wrong-version Agent fixture. It asserts acp_turn_failed, ensure_session, observed version 2, no session/prompt, no host output and no successful terminal event. The retained 105-test run and final release both show that specific case executed, not skipped; their opt-in path resolves the exact repaired public entry. The stricter fake entry is no longer the sole protection for this defect.

The public-entry repair leaves cancellation, permission handling, event drain and failure-phase code intact. Source tracing preserves the CLI fallback requirement of auth-required plus structured ensure_session plus a proven stopped writer boundary; unsupported-version and late auth failures cannot enter that fallback. The retained related-source run covers observed normal v1, unobserved refusal, session-init auth with an absent version, late auth phase turn, and cancellation before and during the prompt. Its 58 tests passed, and all four bound related-source files still match their before/after hashes.

I verified all 15 retained files in the protocol root/final indexes against their recorded byte lengths and SHA-256 values. The narrow and final release snapshots each bind 172 sources, with equal before/after maps and no current source drift. The retained final default-concurrency release reports 737 Node tests and 104 Hook tests passing, zero failures/skips, and zero audit vulnerabilities. This review adds no new blocking code finding within the direct-parent repair delta.
limitations: The refusal boundary is no session/prompt, not no session effects. ACPX creates session/new before saving the record used for observation; the regression explicitly observes that created session. A session-init authentication failure can therefore have an initialize response inside the SDK while the entry has no saved-record observation and honestly reports null.

The direct parent's three P2 records, review-spec-001, review-spec-002 and review-tests-001, remain nonblocking retained scope. This delta does not close the bridge release/Provider wording, capability-advertisement equivalence, or broader integrated normal/denial/cancel coverage concern, and does not authorize their automatic repair.

The earlier full-release evidence-layout failure remains retained. The later unchanged-source release failed with child status null rather than 1 at review-wait.test.cjs:1072; its raw output did not report the child error/signal, so the cause remains unclassified. The exact targeted replay and subsequent full release passed without implementation/assertion changes; neither result establishes that the original failure was harmless. The author's inconsistent future observation timestamp is not used as freshness evidence.

Reviewer scope deviation, excluded from acceptance evidence: I authored five transient local disconnect probes instead of using an existing fixture. The shell invocation was rtk proxy node - with an inline orchestration script; each iteration spawned the existing /tmp/ubp-acpx-protocol-root-z4cncgah/runtime/acpx_delegate_entry.cjs using process.execPath. Its request supplied agent_argv=[process.execPath, '-e', reviewer-authored inline fake-Agent source, localhostPort, trial]. There is no existing fixture path for that inline Agent. The existing entry resolved /Users/rocky243/.local/share/agent-delegation/runtime/node_modules/acpx/dist/runtime.js, version 0.13.2. The ephemeral orchestrator used a local TCP socket for instance counts and traces and reported five single-instance typed AGENT_DISCONNECTED failures with phase turn and observed version 1; it did not reproduce a reconnect bypass. No probe, implementation or test file was persisted. These reviewer-authored diagnostics exceeded the Owner's implementation/test-author role boundary and are not credited to ZCode/Kimi/CC or used as formal repair, regression, qualification or acceptance proof. No further probes were authored.

No full suite was rerun by this reviewer; the formal validation claims above come from independently hash-checked retained raw evidence and current source inspection. No Provider qualification, installation, commit, task completion or canonical qualification publication was performed or inferred. The repaired task-owned entry and its tested copy do not by themselves prove the installed Host path was updated.
